name: Moped
description: A limited-speed motor-driven cycle with wheels under 20 inches that can't exceed 30 mph on level ground, with or without pedals; ITD caps an electric one at 1,500 W, the motor limit of the statute's clause for one without pedals.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels, each less than 20 inches in diameter
Its motor can't propel it faster than 30 mph on level ground
The general clause doesn't require pedals and sets no motor power limit, only the 30 mph cap; a combustion engine is held to 50 cc with an automatic drive

A second clause also takes an electric one with no pedals, an automatic transmission and a motor under 2 gross brake horsepower (1,500 W) that met federal motor vehicle safety standards for motor-driven cycles as manufactured; ITD's titling chart draws the electric moped line at 1,500 W
Not an electric-assisted bicycle; a bike over the e-bike limits is a moped only if it fits this definition
One that can go faster than 30 mph is not a moped, and is a motor-driven cycle or motorcycle if it meets federal safety standards
Not titled, and ITD does not register it or issue it a license plate
No motorcycle endorsement needed to ride one
Not among the vehicles Idaho's under-18 helmet law covers
